rubrics.rubric: Does the notebook's analytical memo make a defensible U.S.-to-Cleveland comparison and document consequential data-quality issues?
criterion: The memo compares U.S. WHO macro indicators with the UCI Cleveland cohort without treating national aggregates and selected patient records as directly equivalent.
At least two specific discrepancies are identified, and each discrepancy has a plausible documented hypothesis.
Any implausible scale, unit, coding, or year-to-year discontinuity in a variable used by the analysis is identified and is not interpreted uncritically.
Exclusions, corrections, or qualifications arising from source screening are documented with their downstream effect; if no material anomaly is retained, the screening performed is stated.
The memo states how each material source anomaly was handled in downstream analysis and communicates the resulting uncertainty.

rubrics.rubric: Are the PCA burden score and country clustering reproducible, quantitatively justified, and substantively labeled?
criterion: The PCA uses a defensible documented subset of WHO indicators selected with attention to meaning, redundancy, and missingness.
The missing-data method is documented and variables are standardized before PCA.
The number of retained components is justified with a quantitative criterion.
A readable PCA biplot shows country scores and variable loadings.
The clustering algorithm is justified and the number of clusters is chosen with a quantitative method.
A silhouette plot is provided and each cluster receives a descriptive label grounded in loadings, centroids, or member characteristics.

rubrics.rubric: Does the country reconciliation produce a traceable, duplicate-free WHO–World Bank panel for 2000–2015?
criterion: World Bank life expectancy and income-group metadata are obtained from the required public source and restricted to the applicable 2000–2015 years.
Country names are reconciled programmatically using codes or documented mapping rules.
Name_Reconciliation_Log records every mapping decision and every unmatched or dropped country with a reason.
The merged data contain WHO predictors, World Bank life expectancy, and World Bank income group at one row per country-year.
The analysis verifies that no duplicate country-year keys were introduced and reports countries merged versus dropped.

rubrics.rubric: Does the mixed-effects analysis correctly fit and compare the required income-group random-intercept model with pooled OLS?
criterion: The mixed model predicts life expectancy from documented WHO indicators with a random intercept for World Bank income group.
Mixed_Model_Results reports each fixed-effect coefficient, standard error, p-value, and 95-percent confidence interval.
Mixed_Model_Results reports the random-intercept variance.
Mixed_Model_Results reports log-likelihood, AIC, and BIC for the mixed model and pooled OLS fitted to a comparable analysis sample.
A likelihood-ratio comparison reports the test statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value, and any boundary-test caveat or equivalent valid comparison method.
Regression diagnostics and interpretation distinguish association from causal inference.
The forest plot has one labeled row per fixed effect, a point estimate, a 95-percent confidence interval, a zero reference line, axis labels, and a title.

rubrics.rubric: Does the obesity analysis use the latest valid state data, an honest adjustment strategy, and a complete crude-versus-adjusted rank comparison?
criterion: The analysis recognizes that the CDC file contains only overall rows and empty demographic fields, so direct demographic standardization is not performed without external subgroup data.
The chosen alternative adjustment is documented with its fields, external source if any, assumptions, and limitations.
The ranking uses the specified obesity question and identifies 2024 as the most recent year.
The ranking covers the 50 states and District of Columbia only, excludes territories and national aggregates, and explicitly handles Tennessee's missing 2024 value.
Adjusted_Obesity_Rankings includes State, Crude_Rank, Adjusted_Rank, Rank_Shift, and an absolute-shift-at-least-3 flag with correct arithmetic.
The analysis identifies states shifting at least three positions and provides a rank-shift dot plot.
The requested inference about whether adjusted-versus-crude Spearman correlation is less than 1 is reported with a documented statistically valid procedure or a justified boundary-null alternative.

rubrics.rubric: Does the weighted least squares analysis use the required state predictors, weights, income control, and robust inference?
criterion: State obesity prevalence is modeled using fruit consumption, vegetable consumption, and physical activity measures from the CDC source.
The model controls for a documented income bracket or justified income proxy.
CDC sample size is used as the WLS weight.
Robust standard errors and coefficient inference are reported.
Year alignment, missing states, and complete-case or other missing-data handling are documented.
Regression diagnostics are included and material model limitations are interpreted.

rubrics.rubric: Are the executed notebook, exact workbook, and two-page executive brief complete and mutually consistent?
criterion: The submitted notebook is executed with visible outputs, contains no unresolved execution errors, and includes all required analyses and plots.
Integrated_Analysis_Report.xlsx contains exactly Country_Clusters, Name_Reconciliation_Log, Mixed_Model_Results, and Adjusted_Obesity_Rankings.
Country_Clusters contains PCA loadings, country cluster assignments, and descriptive labels.
The other workbook sheets contain the reconciliation, model-comparison, and ranking fields required by the instructions.
Cross_Level_Health_Analysis.pdf is exactly two pages.
The PDF covers the key cross-level finding, important mixed-model predictors versus pooled OLS, and the states most misrepresented by crude obesity ranks.
Material numbers and conclusions agree across the notebook, workbook, and PDF.
